    Opposite duals of finite projective modules #

    For a left module M over a possibly noncommutative semiring R, the dual Hom_R(M, R) is a left Rᵐᵒᵖ-module, with scalars acting on the values on the right. This file proves that this dual is finite projective when M is finite projective. In particular, the duals of the projectives in a finite projective presentation are again finite projectives, as required when forming the Auslander–Bridger transpose.

    Main results #

    • EFiniteCharacterizations.oppositeDual_free: the opposite dual of a finite free module is free.
    • EFiniteCharacterizations.oppositeDual_projective: the opposite dual of a finite projective module is projective.
    • EFiniteCharacterizations.oppositeDual_finite: the opposite dual of a finite projective module is finite.

    References #

    • M. Auslander, M. Bridger, Stable module theory, Mem. Amer. Math. Soc. 94 (1969), Section 2.1.

    The dual of a finite free left module is free over the opposite semiring.

    theorem EFiniteCharacterizations.exists_sum_dual_smul_eq {R : Type u_1} {M : Type u_2} [Semiring R] [AddCommMonoid M] [Module R M] [Module.Finite R M] [Module.Projective R M] :
    ∃ (n : ℕ) (b : Fin n → M) (φ : Fin n → Module.Dual R M), ∀ (x : M), ∑ j : Fin n, (φ j) x • b j = x

    Dual basis for a finite projective module. There are finitely many elements bⱼ and functionals φⱼ with x = ∑ⱼ φⱼ(x) • bⱼ for every x.

    Module.Projective Rᵐᵒᵖ (Module.Dual R M)
